title: Distance from the army band and fear of litter work
summary: He never got close to the army band musicians and admits he feared litter work; he had wanted the Air Force or tanks.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What did you do with the litter bearer, did your music find any expression at all? Were they interested in your experience as a young player? Did you talk about it or was it an almost musicless period?

nobody that I could relate to in the music area; I never got close to anybody, because away from the place where we played, I was away from it totally and I could only manage to get down there maybe one or two days a week and for perhaps an hour at a time, so I never got close to the guys in the band and I didn't play much with them, just a few occasions. The fact that they wanted me was important; I guess that's what kept bringing me back.
But I did recognize the fact that I didn't want to leave my outfit to join the band. I think originally I was probably afraid to be a litter bearer.
That gets right into the thick of the action.
You better believe it. The thought of it scared the hell out of me. Well, I don't think I was any different than anybody else, everybody in the army was scared stiff.
I guess that was in no way an expression of your medical background.

I've often wondered why they took me for that, because I didn't pick-- when you're offered three choices I didn't opt for the band--any of the choices. I think number one I wanted the Air Force, number two I think I wanted tanks and not music.
But you didn't own a private airplane?
No. I don't know why the hell I picked it that way either. I might have had a reason then.
Sometimes those reasons get lost very quickly.
